value.name: Rosa demands a room in the house
value.description: Rosa states that she wants a named room in the house, with her own key, for as long as she wants it.
evidence: I would like, in whatever arrangement you make between you, for there to be a room in it for me, named in the document, with a key that is mine and not loaned to me, for as long as I want it.

value.name: Rosa offers her share for one dollar
value.description: Rosa proposes to assign her third to whichever sibling keeps the house in exchange for one dollar.
evidence: In exchange for that, I will assign my third to whichever of you keeps the house, for one dollar.

value.name: Rosa asserts she has not consulted a lawyer
value.description: Rosa emphasizes that she has not spoken to any lawyer and is speaking on her own behalf.
evidence: I have spoken to no lawyer. I am speaking now.

value.name: Rosa insists on her right to speak
value.description: Rosa declares that she will continue speaking if anyone tells her she is wrong to do so.
evidence: I will speak again if you tell me I am wrong to speak.

value.name: Silence falls over the room
value.description: After Rosa's declaration, the room falls into an intense silence that Asha experiences as the largest she has ever heard.
evidence: It was, Asha thought, the largest silence she had heard in this house, and the largest silence she had heard in any house in many years.

value.name: Lucia addresses Rosa by name
value.description: Lucia breaks the silence by speaking Rosa's name.

value.name: Lucia objects to Rosa's proposal
value.description: Lucia tells Rosa that she cannot make the arrangement she has proposed.

value.name: Rosa refuses to back down
value.description: Rosa responds that she is already doing what Lucia says she cannot do.

value.name: Rosa explains her motives and family situation
value.description: Rosa explains that she is old, has family elsewhere, has enough savings, and does not want the burden of owning the building.
evidence: I am sixty-eight years old. I have a sister in Camden and three nieces and a savings account that is larger than your brother thinks it is and smaller than your sister thinks it is. I do not need a building. I need a room. The building is too much for me.

value.name: Rosa compares herself to their mother
value.description: Rosa says the house was too much for their mother as well, and that their mother never admitted it.
evidence: The building was too much for your mother and she would not say so. I am saying so.

value.name: Rosa reveals their mother asked her to prevent conflict
value.description: Rosa reveals that their mother asked her in February to keep Lucia and her sibling from destroying each other over the house.
evidence: I am saying so because she asked me, in February, to make sure the two of you did not destroy each other over this house

value.name: Rosa frames the house as belonging to one sibling
value.description: Rosa argues that the best way to avoid conflict is for the house to belong to one of the siblings rather than be split into three parts.
evidence: the way to make sure of that is for the house to belong to one of you and not to be divided into three pieces of which one piece is mine.

value.name: Rosa distinguishes legal codicil from personal wish
value.description: Rosa explains that the codicil was for legal purposes, while this conversation is about her personal wish.
evidence: The codicil was for the law. This conversation is for the wish.
